text:
I never gave a lock of my hair to any man,

my beloved, except the one I offer you now,

and, thoughtfully, along all its somber

length, I wind it around my fingers.


Take it. My days of youth have passed;

my hair no longer trembles at my joyful step,

nor do I fasten in it the rose or myrtle shoots,

as girls usually do: now it can only, on pale


cheeks, shade the traces of my weeping,

and it has grown used to coming loose when sorrow,

with its art, bends the forehead. I feared the funereal


scissors would cut it first, and your

love has prevailed. Take it. Pure as before, you will find

the kiss my mother left in it when she died.

translation.title: I Never Gave a Lock of My Hair to Any Man
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the lock of hair as intimate gift, mourning relic, and maternal trace.
